newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers mostly unchanged.

text.p: Most soybean basis offers were unchanged Wednesday and dealers reported only a modest amount of buyer interest following huge losses on the Chicago Board of Trade this week.
"I'm seeing a little bit of stuff being bought here for July," said a dealer in the U.S. southeast. "These prices look pretty good to people."
CBOT July soymeal was down $2.50 at $241.70 a ton.
Supplies of soymeal remained heavy in some Midwest markets, and cash traders reported a number of locations that still had unsold soymeal in railcars waiting for shipment.
Dealers continued to speculate that the market's build-up of supply would cause some crushers to slow down or stop production over the three-day Independence Day holiday weekend beginning on Friday.
Also, some crushers will begin to take scheduled downtime for maintenance beginning this month.
The National Oilseed Processors Association will release its weekly crush on Monday at 0730 CDT instead of Friday because of the holiday weekend.
